div.head: I Atr 2
div.ab: ⁊ gif þeowman fúl wurðe æt þam ordale, mearcie man hine æt ðam forman cyrre.
And gyf ðeowman ful wurðe æt [þam ordale, mearcie man hine æt] ðam forman cyrran.
Et si seruus culpabilis appareat in ordalio, signetur in prima uice.
[Be ðeowmen ðe ful wyrþe.] And gyf ðeowman ful wurðe æt þam ordale, mearcie man hine æt ðam forman cyrran.
(Vom Unfreien, der schuldig befunden wird. Ld) Und wenn ein Unfreier beim Ordal schuldig befunden wird, so werde er beim ersten Male gebrandmarkt.
(Of the slave who is found guilty. Ld) And if a slave is found guilty at the ordeal, let him be branded the first time.
And if a slave is found guilty at the ordeal, he shall be branded on the first occasion.

Strenger als Æthelstan; vgl. Gl Ordal 32e. f.; unfrei 19. 21k.—Den Satz wiederholt II Cn 32
Stricter than Æthelstan; cf. Gl Ordal 32e. f.; unfrei 19. 21k.—The sentence is repeated by II Cn 32
Vgl. Gl Brandmarken. Da der Unfreie vermögenslos, tritt sofort Leibesstrafe ein.—Zur Form cyrran in B, die dieser Schreiber in II Cn 32, 1 wiederholt, vgl. Wb S. 48 Sp. 2
Cf. Gl Brandmarken. Since the unfree man has no property, corporal punishment follows at once.—On the form cyrran in B, which this scribe repeats in II Cn 32, 1, cf. Wb p. 48 col. 2

The punishment, as Liebermann points out, is more severe than that inflicted by Æthelstan (see II As. 19). For later instances of branding see E.H.R., 1895, p. 726; Bateson, Borough Customs, i. 77 f. and note.
Liebermann (ii. p. 48, Col. 2, No. 5) notes the occasional use of weak declension forms in MS B, e.g. cyrran here and in II Cn. 32, 1; of eardan, II Cn. 3; on wintran, In. 38.
